items.title: The Four Right Efforts, the Four Bases of Supernormal Power, and the Four Dhyānas as States of Settled Mind

items.zh: 又有四種欲勤為先，觀察過患及與對治以為依止，能斷現行諸不善法，及斷彼繫；能得善法，及能增長。又有四種為欲住心為得勝定修方便者，心住如意能生長門。一、樂出離欲；二、受持讀誦，悔過精進；三、能取賢善定相之心；四、住空閑處，觀察諸法。又有四種心定心住。一、有尋有伺有喜心住；二、無尋無伺有喜心住；三、無尋無伺離喜心住；四、捨念清淨，超度一切苦樂心住。
items.en: There are also four things, aspiration and diligence coming first, taking as their basis the observation of faults and their antidotes, capable of severing manifest unwholesome phenomena and severing their bondage, and capable of attaining wholesome phenomena and increasing them. There are also four things, for one who wishes to settle the mind and cultivates the means to attain superior concentration, that are the gateway through which the mind, settled, is able to grow at will: first, delighting in renouncing desire; second, receiving, retaining, reciting, confessing wrongdoing, and diligence; third, a mind able to grasp the excellent sign of concentration; fourth, dwelling in a secluded place and observing phenomena. There are also four settlings of a concentrated mind: first, the settling accompanied by applied and sustained thought and by joy; second, the settling free of applied and sustained thought yet still accompanied by joy; third, the settling free of applied and sustained thought and free of joy; fourth, the settling of purified equanimity and mindfulness, transcending both pleasure and pain entirely.

items.title: The Four Noble Truths as Cause and Effect, Four Kinds of Bondage Through Perception, and the Four Immeasurables

items.zh: 又有四種所知真實。染污、清淨二品別故，建立四種。若能了知、善了知者，能斷見、修所斷一切煩惱。一、染污品果真實，二、彼品因真實，三、清淨品果真實，四、彼品因真實。又有四種想為先戲論縛。一、於小欲中想為先戲論縛，二、於大色中想為先戲論縛，三、於無量空、識無邊處想為先戲論縛，四、於無所有處想為先戲論縛。又有四法，於諸有情對治恚害不樂欲貪。善修習時能生大福，能趣離欲。一、慈，二、悲，三、喜，四、捨。
items.en: There are also four kinds of reality to be known, established by the distinction between the defiled and pure classes: knowing them, and knowing them well, one is able to sever all afflictions cut by the paths of seeing and cultivation. First, the reality of the defiled class's fruit; second, the reality of that class's cause; third, the reality of the pure class's fruit; fourth, the reality of that class's cause. There are also four bonds of discursive proliferation with perception coming first: first, the bond in small desire; second, the bond in vast form; third, the bond in the boundless spheres of space and consciousness; fourth, the bond in the sphere of nothingness. There are also four things that counter hostility, cruelty, displeasure, and craving towards sentient beings; cultivated well, they generate great merit and lead towards freedom from desire: first, loving-kindness; second, compassion; third, sympathetic joy; fourth, equanimity.

items.title: The Four Formless Attainments, and the Four Noble Lineages of Contentment That Sustain Genuine Practice

items.zh: 又有四法超過色界，令成遠分。謂空處、識處、無所有處、非想非非想處。又有四種，為令解脫速得圓滿，勤修行者聖解脫欲勝任持法，為斷四愛增上力故。謂為衣服、飲食、臥具，少有所求，無作無亂，時無虛度，勤修方便；心離散亂，樂斷煩惱、樂修正道。
items.en: There are also four things that transcend the form realm, making it a distant thing: the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception. There are also four things, sought by the diligent practitioner with the noble aspiration for liberation, that powerfully sustain that liberation and bring it swiftly to fulfilment, by the power of severing the four cravings: namely, regarding clothing, food, and bedding — having little desire, free of contrivance and disorder, never idling away the time and diligently cultivating the means [contentment with clothing, with food, and with bedding respectively]; the mind free of distraction, delighting in severing affliction, delighting in cultivating the correct path.

items.title: The Four Fruits Mapped to Exactly Which Fetters They Sever, and the Four Confirmed Purities of a Stream-Enterer

items.zh: 又有四種修習道果諸煩惱斷。一、見所斷煩惱斷，二、修所斷下分結上中品斷，三、即此無餘斷，四、上分結無餘斷。復有四種證預流支，能令行者於佛聖教及善趣中畢竟不動。謂於大師所真覺所生無動心淨。如於大師所，當知於所證法及為證法修證行者所亦爾。如是三種名心清淨。第四一種名色清淨。聖所愛戒所攝故。前之三種、令於聖教無有動搖；最後一種、令於善趣無有動搖。
items.en: There are also four severances of affliction through cultivating the fruits of the path: first, severing what is cut by the path of seeing; second, severing the middle and upper grades of the lower fetters cut by the path of cultivation; third, severing the very remainder of those same lower fetters entirely; fourth, severing the upper fetters entirely. There are also four supports of stream-entry, which cause the practitioner to remain utterly unshaken with regard to the Buddha's sacred teaching and with regard to a favourable rebirth. Namely: towards the Great Teacher, an unshaken purity of mind born of genuine realisation. As towards the Great Teacher, know it is likewise so towards the Dharma realised, and towards those who practice rightly in order to realise that Dharma. These three are called purity of mind. The fourth alone is called purity of form, since it is comprised within the precepts a noble one loves. The first three cause one to remain unshaken with regard to the sacred teaching; the last causes one to remain unshaken with regard to a favourable rebirth.

items.title: The Four Causes of Stream-Entry Restated, and Four Kinds of Knowledge Comprehending All Wisdom

items.zh: 又有四種證預流支。一、於說法師及教授者能善承事，無所違犯；二、無倒聽聞師所說法及教授法；三、於所聞法能正思惟及善通達；四、成辦所修。又有四智攝一切智。一、唯無漏，於諸法中能現見智；二、一向無漏、於諸法中非現見智；三、一向有漏，或如理所引、或不如理所引、或非如理非不如理所引世間智；四、通有漏、無漏他心差別智。
items.en: There are also four causes of stream-entry: first, skilfully attending upon the teacher and instructor without transgression; second, hearing the teacher's teaching and instruction without distortion; third, correctly reflecting on and thoroughly penetrating what has been heard; fourth, accomplishing what is thereby cultivated. There are also four kinds of knowledge comprehending all knowledge: first, purely uncontaminated knowledge that directly perceives phenomena; second, uniformly uncontaminated knowledge of phenomena that does not directly perceive them; third, uniformly contaminated worldly knowledge, whether rightly guided, wrongly guided, or neither; fourth, knowledge of others' minds, common to both the contaminated and the uncontaminated.

items.title: Applying the Four Truths to Every Link of Dependent Origination, and the Four Practical Means to Actually Sever Affliction

items.zh: 又有四種於轉還品真實能取智，能盡諸漏。一、轉品果真實智，二、轉品因真實智，三、還品果真實智，四、還品因真實智。又有四法，能令信者為斷煩惱修正方便。一、相續殷重作用精進。二、正知行念，三、奢摩他，四、毘鉢舍那。
items.en: There are also four kinds of genuine, apprehending knowledge regarding the flux and return classes, capable of exhausting all outflows: first, genuine knowledge of the fruit of the flux class; second, genuine knowledge of the cause of the flux class; third, genuine knowledge of the fruit of the return class; fourth, genuine knowledge of the cause of the return class. There are also four things that let one of genuine faith cultivate the correct means to sever affliction: first, sustained, earnest, diligent effort; second, correct knowledge, conduct, and mindfulness; third, calm; fourth, insight.

items.zh: 又有四種能通達法，能盡上漏所依足迹。謂為得聖道，修有漏慧；既得道已，缺諸煩惱及缺諸事；無餘永斷諸煩惱事；如所得道轉更修習。

items.title: The Four Formless Aggregates Working as One, and Four Concrete Protections That Keep a Practitioner Loving the Teaching

items.zh: 又有四法展轉相應，有行、有緣，和合而轉、同一緣轉。謂受、想、行、識。又有四護，能令已入佛聖教者愛樂聖教。一者、命護，二者、力護，三者、心煩惱護，四者、正方便護。
items.en: There are also four phenomena mutually corresponding, each with its own mode of activity yet sharing an object, arising together and operating on a single shared object: namely, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness. There are also four protections that let one who has entered the Buddha's sacred teaching continue to love it: first, protection of livelihood; second, protection of strength; third, protection from mental affliction; fourth, protection of correct effort.

blocks.text: Today continues the fours, through the core of the thirty-seven factors of awakening, the four noble lineages of contentment, and the four factors of stream-entry. Most are familiar; the treatise's contribution is to say exactly what each counters.

subs.head: Right efforts, bases of power, dhyānas

blocks.text: The **four right efforts** (四正勤): to prevent and abandon unwholesome states, and to arouse and maintain wholesome ones. The *Pīxún jì* maps "severing manifest unwholesome states" onto what has already arisen, and "severing their bondage" onto what has not yet arisen, the seeds. The **four bases of supernormal power** (四神足): desire, effort, mind, and investigation. The four dhyānas as "states of settled mind": only the fourth transcends pleasure and pain. Venerable Miào Jìng notes that this treatise says the first dhyāna has not yet removed pain (Day 80), unlike the *Vibhāṣā*.

The four noble truths as cause and effect. "Knowing them, and knowing them well" severs affliction. Venerable Miào Jìng: knowing is the wisdom of hearing and reflection; "knowing well" is the wisdom of cultivation. The four immeasurables counter hostility, cruelty, displeasure, and craving (Day 90).

The **four noble lineages** (四聖種): contentment with robes, contentment with food, contentment with lodging, and delight in abandoning and cultivating. The *Pīxún jì* assigns "little desire" to robes, "no contrivance" to food, and "never idling" to bedding. Contentment is the lineage, the family resemblance, of noble ones.

subs.head: Four fruits and what they cut

blocks.text: Each fruit is defined by the fetters it severs. Stream-entry cuts the three fetters (self-view, doubt, grasping at precepts). Once-return cuts, as Master Cháng Bǎi explains, the six coarser of the nine grades of desire-realm craving and hostility. Non-return cuts all five lower fetters. Arhatship cuts the five higher.

The four causes of stream-entry: associating with good people, hearing the true Dharma, proper attention, and practice in accord with the Dharma. Venerable Miào Jìng on hearing "without distortion": "Set all your own opinions aside, like a blank sheet of paper, and receive the teaching." A stream-enterer has four **confirmed purities**: unshakable faith in the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and the precepts dear to the noble.

One of them is "correct knowledge, conduct, and mindfulness". Venerable Miào Jìng compares correct knowledge to "a police officer, monitoring whether people's conduct is lawful": clear comprehension watches what the mind is doing.

Feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness work together on "the same object, not the same mode". (Day 1's "one object, many aspects".) Four protections keep a practitioner loving the teaching.

quiz.q: The right efforts sever "manifest unwholesome phenomena and their bondage." How do the lectures map this to arisen and unarisen evil, and how does the reading note differ?
options: severing the manifest = arisen (restraint); severing bondage = unarisen, the seeds; the note reverses them
quiz.why: The *Pixunji*: severing manifest unwholesome phenomena concerns the arisen; severing their bondage concerns the unarisen. Master Cháng Bǎi: severing the manifest is restraint through precepts. Venerable Miào Jìng: the bondage is the seeds. The note reverses this.

quiz.q: Only the fourth settling "transcends pleasure and pain." Comparing the Mahāvibhāṣā with this treatise, does the first dhyāna overcome pain, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: both say pleasure only in the fourth
the Vibhāṣā says the first dhyāna already escapes pain; this treatise specifically says it has not yet removed pain
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The *Mahāvibhāṣā* says the first dhyāna already breaks out of pain, but this treatise specifically says the first dhyāna has not yet removed it." Master Cháng Bǎi: the fourth is free of the three calamities and eight disturbances.

quiz.q: The treatise says "knowing them, and knowing them well" severs afflictions. How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish the two?
options: knowing is the wisdom of hearing and reflection; knowing well is the wisdom of cultivation, which surpasses them — hence "well"
knowing is the Buddha's, knowing well the bodhisattva's
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "'Knowing well' is the wisdom of cultivation — it surpasses the wisdom of hearing and reflection, hence 'well.'" The reading note maps the two onto the paths of seeing and cultivation instead.

quiz.q: The four immeasurables counter hostility, cruelty, displeasure, and craving. How does the Pixunji pair them?
options: love counters craving, compassion hostility, joy cruelty, equanimity displeasure
love counters hostility, compassion cruelty, joy displeasure, equanimity craving and hostility
quiz.why: The *Pixunji*: love counters hostility, operating without injury; compassion counters cruelty, removing others' pain; joy counters displeasure, rejoicing in others' happiness; equanimity counters craving and hostility. Venerable Miào Jìng: "displeasure" is envy.

quiz.q: The second severance is "the middle and upper grades of the lower fetters." Which fruit is that, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: once-return — of nine grades, the six coarse and middle grades are severed
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: each of upper, middle, and lower is again split in three — nine grades for craving and hostility; severing six of them, the coarse and middle, one realises the second fruit. Venerable Miào Jìng agrees.

quiz.q: What other name does Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the Pixunji, give the four causes of stream-entry in §22?
options: the four right practices: associating with good people, hearing the true Dharma, proper attention, practice in accord with the Dharma
quiz.why: The *Pixunji*: associating with good people, hearing the true Dharma, proper attention, and practice in accord with the Dharma are called the four right practices. The reading note's "four reliances" is the wrong term.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain hearing the teaching "without distortion"?
options: setting all one's own opinions aside, like a blank sheet, to receive the teaching
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Set all your own opinions aside, like a blank sheet of paper, and receive the teaching he gives — that is hearing without distortion." Even bodhisattvas of virtually equal awakening still listen to the Buddha.
